articles.title: Gold, silver or steel: What should you actually buy on Dhanteras?
articles.summary: When you think about stepping out to shop on Dhanteras, gold is usually the first thing that pops into your head.
articles.body: When you think about stepping out to shop on Dhanteras, gold is usually the first thing that pops into your head. But silver and even a humble steel utensil have a long-standing place in the celebrations, too.So, how do you navigate the annual dilemma? Should you spend on gold, pick up a few silver coins or simply bring home a new vessel for your kitchen?For many families, buying gold is an annual tradition. Others prefer silver, while plenty of households stick to something practical for the home. And with gold prices hovering near record highs, people are understandably thinking twice before making a purchase.Here's a look at how gold, silver and steel compare, both culturally and practically, so you can decide what makes sense for your budget.Why do we buy metals on Dhanteras in the first place?Dhanteras, also known as Dhantrayodashi, falls on the thirteenth lunar day of Krishna Paksha during the Hindu month of Kartik. The festival is associated with Goddess Lakshmi, Lord Kubera and Lord Dhanvantari.Lord Dhanvantari is revered as the deity of health and Ayurveda. According to the story of Samudra Manthan, or the churning of the cosmic ocean, he emerged carrying a kalash filled with amrita, the nectar of immortality. This association with a vessel is one reason why bringing home new metal utensils became part of the Dhanteras tradition.The Bhagavata Purana (Canto 8, Chapter 8) describes Dhanvantari's emergence during the churning of the ocean. However, it doesn't specifically instruct people to buy gold, silver or steel. These shopping customs developed over time around the festival's association with wealth and prosperity.That's worth remembering. Buying a particular metal is a popular tradition, not a religious rule that every household must follow.1. Gold: The traditional favouriteGold is easily the most popular Dhanteras purchase, especially among families who see the occasion as an opportunity to add to their jewellery collection or long-term savings.The metal has long been associated with Goddess Lakshmi, wealth and good fortune. But there's a financial reason behind its popularity, too. Gold is traded globally and attracts demand from investors, central banks and jewellery buyers.According to the World Gold Council's Gold as a Strategic Asset 2026 report, gold has historically helped diversify investment portfolios and preserve value over longer periods. That said, its price doesn't always move upwards. Gold can experience sharp fluctuations, with annual price movements sometimes approaching 30%.What should you buy?24-karat gold coins: A good option if purity and easy storage are your priorities.22-karat jewellery: Suitable if you want something you can wear while retaining precious-metal value.Gold bars: Worth considering if your primary intention is investment.One thing to remember: jewellery comes with making charges, which you may not recover when you sell it. If you're buying gold purely as an investment, coins or bars may be more suitable.2. Silver: The more affordable alternativeIf you don't want to spend a large amount on gold, silver is another popular choice for Dhanteras.From Lakshmi-Ganesha coins and small bars to jewellery and puja utensils, there's plenty to choose from across different budgets. For many families, buying a silver coin, worshipping it during Diwali and keeping it safely is an annual ritual.But silver isn't simply a cheaper version of gold.The World Gold Council points out that silver tends to be more volatile than gold. A large part of its demand comes from industries such as solar energy, electronics and electrical equipment. This means its price is influenced by industrial activity and global economic conditions, apart from jewellery and investment demand.What should you buy?999 fine silver coins: Check the purity details before purchasing.925 sterling silver jewellery: A popular option for everyday accessories.Silver utensils and puja items: Useful additions to a household collection.A quick tip: Look for BIS hallmarking and the HUID number when buying eligible hallmarked silver articles. You can use the BIS Care app to verify the six-digit identification code before making the purchase.3. Steel: Does a kitchen vessel count as a Dhanteras purchase?This is where family traditions can differ.Stainless steel doesn't have the investment value of gold or silver, but bringing home new utensils is a common way of celebrating Dhanteras.The practice is often linked to Lord Dhanvantari's amrita kalash. Over time, families began buying new vessels made of brass, copper, silver and, eventually, stainless steel.There are regional differences, though. Some households avoid buying iron or steel on Dhanteras because of traditional associations with Shani Dev. Others have no such restriction and make a point of purchasing new kitchenware every year. There is no universal scriptural prohibition against buying steel.From a practical standpoint, stainless steel is a sensible choice. It's durable, relatively affordable and useful for everyday cooking and serving.The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has a dedicated standard, IS 14756, for stainless steel utensils. It covers requirements such as material quality, thickness, workmanship and safety.What should you buy?A stainless steel dinner set for everyday use.Serving bowls, platters or cooking pots.Storage containers for your kitchen.Just check for the ISI mark and avoid choosing utensils purely because they're cheap or look shiny.What do ancient Hindu texts actually say about buying metals?The religious references behind Dhanteras are worth looking at more closely.The Bhagavata Purana (Canto 8, Chapter 8, verses 33–35) describes Lord Dhanvantari emerging from the ocean during Samudra Manthan, carrying a pot of amrita. The account establishes his association with Lord Vishnu, healing and Ayurveda.The Skanda Purana is also associated with the tradition of lighting a lamp for Lord Yama on Trayodashi, commonly known as Yamadeepdaan. The ritual is observed with the belief that it helps ward off untimely death.But there's no ancient shopping checklist that says every household must purchase gold or silver on this day.As discussed by author Amish Tripathi in a conversation about Indian cultural traditions, buying gold on Dhanteras is largely a folk custom that developed over time rather than a strict scriptural requirement.So, whether you bring home a small silver coin or a gold bar, you can still celebrate the festival without making an expensive purchase.When should you shop? Check the PanchangIf your family follows auspicious timings for festival shopping and puja, checking the local Panchang is a good idea.For Dhanteras on November 6, 2026, the timings listed for Mumbai are:Trayodashi Tithi begins: 10:30 am on November 6, 2026.Trayodashi Tithi ends: 10:47 am on November 7, 2026.Lakshmi-Kubera evening puja muhurat: 6:35 pm to 8:35 pm on November 6, 2026.These timings are location-specific. The auspicious window for buying metals may also differ from the evening puja muhurat, so check your city's Panchang before planning your purchase.You can refer to a Panchang for the local timings.Gold vs silver vs steel: How do they compare?FactorGoldSilverSteelTraditional appealVery highVery highDepends on family customCostHighModerateAffordableInvestment valueEstablished precious-metal assetPrecious-metal asset, more volatileNo meaningful investment valueEveryday useJewelleryJewellery and puja itemsCooking and servingWhat to checkBIS hallmark and HUIDBIS hallmark and HUIDISI markSo, what should you buy this Dhanteras?There's no single right answer. It really comes down to your budget, family traditions and what you actually need.Choose gold if you can comfortably afford it and want to add to your family's long-term savings or jewellery collection.Choose silver if you'd like to bring home a precious metal without spending as much as you would on gold. Coins and puja items are particularly popular choices.Choose steel if practicality matters more to you. A good-quality cooking pot or dinner set is something your family can use every day.And don't let shopping pressure dictate how much you spend. Dhanteras is about welcoming prosperity, health and good fortune into your home. There's little point in taking on unnecessary financial stress just to keep up with a tradition.Whether it's a silver coin, a sturdy steel vessel or a gold pendant, buy what works for your home and your pocket. That's reason enough to celebrate.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: ‘Vote gone, rights gone’: Rahul alleges BJP conspiracy in schemes linked with voter ID instead of Aadhaar
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday launched a sharp attack on the Centre over Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh's announcement that voter
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday launched a sharp attack on the Centre over Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh's announcement that voter ID cards would be used instead of Aadhaar to identify beneficiaries of social welfare programmes under the ministry of panchayati raj.Calling the move a "conspiracy", the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha alleged that linking welfare benefits to voter IDs could put people's access to government schemes at risk.In a post on X, Rahul claimed that the announcement was part of a wider attempt to remove names from electoral rolls through the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). He alleged that millions of names were being deleted under the exercise and that those most critical of the BJP were being targeted."Modi government minister's announcement - Benefits of schemes will now be determined not by Aadhaar, but by Voter ID. The conspiracy runs very deep—take your time to understand it. Under the guise of SIR, millions of names are being struck off voter lists—if not stopped, even more will be removed. Whose names are being targeted the most? Those who are furious with the BJP," Rahul said.He also accused the Election Commission of India (ECI) of colluding with the BJP, alleging that electoral rolls were no longer being maintained by an impartial body. Rahul named Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of being a "Modi government employee" and claiming that his alleged collusion with the BJP in "vote theft" had been exposed with evidence."The preparation is underway to craft such a list where the majority is always BJP's—and now that very list will decide whether you get scheme benefits or not. Anyone who decided yesterday that the BJP must go—will have their names cherry-picked and struck off. Name struck—vote gone. Vote gone—rights gone. And just like that, you'll become invisible citizens of a hijacked democracy—where the people don't elect the government, the government selects its people," he added.Rahul further warned that making voter ID mandatory for welfare benefits could eventually affect access to ration, pensions, MGNREGA wages, housing assistance, scholarships and reservations. He argued that voting rights should not be made a condition for receiving welfare benefits."Today, Panchayati Raj schemes. Tomorrow, rations? Pensions? MGNREGA? Housing? Scholarships? Reservations? This isn't politics to win elections—it's an arrangement to steal elections and a permanent setup to cling to power.Voting is your right, not a condition. A poor person's pension cannot be enslaved to their voter card. This isn't just vote theft—it's rights theft. We won't let this happen," he said.Singh, also known as Lallan Singh, had announced that beneficiaries seeking financial assistance and welfare payments under schemes of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj would need to provide an Elector's Photo Identity Card (EPIC) number and undergo mandatory biometric authentication. The proposed system would use voter ID instead of Aadhaar for identifying beneficiaries.The announcement has raised questions about the scope of the move, as the Ministry of Panchayati Raj does not directly operate schemes involving payments to individual beneficiaries. Aadhaar is currently used for beneficiary identification and payments under several other central government programmes, including rural housing assistance, PM-KISAN and social security pensions.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: SC ends decades-old power tussle, Himachal to get 11,973 MU from Punjab, Haryana
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday settled a decades-old inter-state dispute over unpaid electricity dues from Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB)
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday settled a decades-old inter-state dispute over unpaid electricity dues from Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB) projects, directing Punjab and Haryana to provide Himachal Pradesh with 11,973 million units (MU) of electricity over 20 years. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, along with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, accepted the Centre's proposal to clear the outstanding dues through an energy-based settlement instead of a cash payment.The settlement follows a 2011 Supreme Court verdict that recognised Himachal Pradesh's entitlement to a 7.19 per cent share in the electricity generated by the Bhakra Nangal and Beas hydroelectric projects. The dues date back to 1966, but Punjab and Haryana had not cleared the state's outstanding share for the period before November 2011.Under the arrangement approved by the top court, Punjab and Haryana will provide the electricity over 20 years. The settlement also factors in an adjustment of around Rs 420 crore towards Himachal Pradesh's share of the historical capital costs incurred in building the dams. As a result, the hill state will not have to make any separate payment to Punjab or Haryana.The Centre had earlier proposed that the 13,066 MU in outstanding electricity dues be paid over 15 years, at the rate of 871 MU annually during the lean seasons between October and March. However, the states could not agree on the proposed timeline.Punjab initially opposed the 15-year arrangement and later sought to extend the payment period to 30 years. Himachal Pradesh, on the other hand, wanted the dues cleared within 10 years. The Supreme Court's decision to settle the matter over 20 years brings an end to the prolonged disagreement over the payment schedule.The original electricity arrears were calculated at 13,066 MU by the Central Electricity Authority (CEA). The Centre's proposal had also factored in Himachal Pradesh's liability towards the capital costs of the Bhakra Nangal and Beas projects.According to a report by PTI, the proposal says that Himachal Pradesh's liability was assessed at Rs 420.7 crore, comprising Rs 249.2 crore payable to Punjab and Rs 171.5 crore to Haryana. This represented the state's 7.19 per cent share of the composite of Punjab's outstanding loan-servicing costs for the projects since 1966-67.The Centre had suggested setting off this liability against a portion of the electricity arrears. At the proposed rate of Rs 3.85 per unit, around 1,093 MU would have been adjusted against the capital cost liability.The proposal also provided for the distribution of electricity arrears between Punjab and Haryana in the inter-state ratio of 58:42 for the Bhakra Nangal project and 60:40 for the Beas projects. However, since the states could not reach a consensus on the applicable electricity rate, the Centre recommended settling the dues in energy terms.What was the 2011 Supreme Court verdict?The Supreme Court's 2011 decision fixed Himachal Pradesh's share in the BBMB projects at 7.19 per cent. Punjab's share was set at 51.80 per cent, while Haryana was allocated 37.51 per cent. Rajasthan's share largely remained unchanged, and Chandigarh's share was fixed at 3.50 per cent.The verdict also specified when Himachal Pradesh's entitlement would take effect for the three projects. The state was entitled to a share in the Bhakra project from November 1, 1966, the Dehar project from November 1977 and the Pong Dam project from January 1978.The BBMB has been providing Himachal Pradesh with its 7.19 per cent share of electricity from these projects since November 1, 2011, PTI reported, citing sources. However, Punjab and Haryana had not cleared the outstanding dues for the earlier period, amounting to 13,066 MU.How did the dispute reach the Supreme Court?The dispute dates back to the reorganisation of Punjab under the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966. Himachal Pradesh maintained that, as a successor state, it was entitled to a 7.19 per cent share in the BBMB projects and their electricity generation.After efforts to resolve the disagreement between the neighbouring states failed, Himachal Pradesh approached the Supreme Court in 1996 through an original suit. It sought recognition of its entitlement to a share in the projects and the payment of the corresponding arrears.The Centre subsequently attempted to settle the matter outside court. However, with no agreement emerging between the states, the Supreme Court passed a decree on September 27, 2011, upholding Himachal Pradesh's 7.19 per cent entitlement.The latest order accepting the Centre's energy-based settlement provides a mechanism to clear the accumulated dues and closes a dispute that has remained unresolved for decades.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: UK Henry Nowak murder case: Court increases Vickrum Digwa's minimum term to 25 years after ruling 21-year sentence 'unduly lenient'
articles.summary: The Court of Appeal has increased Vickrum Digwa's minimum term for the murder of student Henry Nowak to 25 years, ruling the previous 21-year sentence as unduly lenient. The decision comes after challenges from both the Attorney General and Digwa regarding the severity of the sentence.
articles.body: Vickrum Digwa, Sikh man who was sentenced to life imprisonment for killing 18-year-old student Henry Nowak in Southampton, will have to serve at least 25 years before becoming eligible for parole after the Court of Appeal increased his minimum term from 21 years.The decision followed a challenge by Attorney General Ellie Reeves, who argued that the original sentence was unduly lenient. Digwa had also appealed against the term, describing it as manifestly excessive. However, the court rejected his challenge and ruled that the original punishment failed to reflect the full seriousness of the offence, according to BBC.Digwa stabbed Nowak with a large dagger on Belmont Road, Southampton, on December 3 last year. The 22-year-old was sentenced to life imprisonment at Southampton Crown Court in June.The appeals were heard on Thursday by Lady Chief Justice Baroness Carr, alongside Mr Justice Nicklin and Mr Justice Wall. Digwa attended the proceedings through a video link from HMP Frankland.In delivering the ruling, Baroness Carr said the trial judge was entitled to set a starting point of 15 years because Digwa had not brought the weapon to the scene with the intention of committing a crime. However, she said the use of a large kirpan required a substantial increase in the minimum term.A kirpan is a religious blade that baptised Sikhs are expected to carry. UK law permits Sikhs to carry such knives in public for religious purposes. Digwa wore a smaller kirpan around his neck but also carried a larger blade secured to his belt, following the practices of the Nihang order.The court said the lawful possession of the weapon did not lessen the seriousness of using it to kill someone. Baroness Carr said the earlier sentence had failed to account adequately for the repeated use of the dagger, the intention to kill and the suffering inflicted on Nowak, as well as the obstruction that followed."It was not only lenient, but unduly so," she said.After accounting for the time Digwa has already spent in custody on remand, he must serve at least 24 years and 190 days before he can be considered for parole, as per the outlet.Nowak's family described the increased sentence as "an important step towards justice" but said it could not compensate for their loss."No sentence, however long, can ever give Henry his life back," the family said in a statement, as cited by BBC.They added that they had been left with "a life sentence of grief", saying there was no reduction in their suffering and no possibility of getting their son back. The family also said their pursuit of justice was continuing and expressed support for an independent rapid review being carried out by Alex Chalk.Attorney General Reeves said the brutality of the killing had deeply affected her and expressed sympathy for Nowak's family."No sentence can ever fill the void left by his loss, and I hope this outcome goes some way towards bringing them the justice they deserve," she said.During the appeal hearing, Jonathan Polnay KC, representing the Attorney General, argued that the original 21-year minimum term did not reflect the seriousness of the crime. He said Digwa had taken advantage of the legal exemption permitting Sikhs to carry religious blades, describing the circumstances as comparable, in some respects, to an abuse of trust.Imran Khan KC, representing Digwa, argued that the trial judge had counted some aggravating factors more than once. He maintained that the original term was already excessive, saying: "To put it pithily, the Attorney General says 21 years was too little. We say it was too much."The appeal judges agreed that certain factors should not have been treated as aggravating circumstances, including the wider impact of the killing on the community, which Digwa had neither anticipated nor intended.Digwa's mother, Kiran Kaur, was sentenced to three years in prison in July for assisting an offender by removing the murder weapon from the scene. She withdrew her challenge against that sentence shortly before Thursday's hearing.Digwa has separately applied for permission to appeal against his murder conviction. That application will be considered independently of the sentencing decision.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: After GOP's midterm rout, Laura Loomer announces 'break' from hosting podcast; not from supporting Trump or offering political comments; cites upcoming wedding as the reason
articles.summary: Far-right political influencer Laura Loomer has announced that she is taking a hiatus from her twice-weekly livestreamed show, Loomer Unleashed, saying
articles.body: Far-right political influencer Laura Loomer has announced that she is taking a hiatus from her twice-weekly livestreamed show, Loomer Unleashed, saying she needs to focus on her personal life, family and upcoming wedding after spending years working almost around the clock to support US President Donald Trump. Loomer made the announcement in a lengthy post on X on Thursday night, November 5, 2026. She clarified that she was not quitting political commentary or withdrawing her support for Trump, but would temporarily stop hosting her show."I’ve been going nonstop supporting President Trump @realDonaldTrump ever since he came down the golden escalator. As many of you know, I am chronically tuned in, online, and I am always working. I am a machine. Some days I work more than 18 hours," she wrote.Explaining her decision, Loomer said she had been neglecting her personal life and relationships because of her work. She said she had been "running on empty for too long" and wanted to establish a healthier balance between her professional commitments and private life."There is more to life than work though, and I am trying to learn that and practice it. It’s been very hard for me to be honest. Very very hard," she said.Loomer said her family, personal life and upcoming wedding had been put on hold because of her work. She also said she wanted to spend more time with her partner and participate in wedding planning."So I’m taking a hiatus from my show @LoomerUnleashed, which I livestream twice a week. I just need to step back, recharge, refocus, and be present in my own life and my own mind with peace and clarity for a little while," she wrote.She also said she wanted to redesign her studio, something she had been postponing for nearly a year because of her professional commitments."I have wanted to redo my studio for a year, but I keep pushing it all off, because that’s what I do. I push things off that matter to me and my happiness to do for others 24/7, and I think I need to change that for a brief moment," she said.Will Laura Loomer stop political commentary?Loomer made it clear that her decision to suspend the show does not mean she is stepping away from politics or her support for Trump. She said she would continue following developments, researching stories and commenting on breaking news."I’ll still be paying attention, fully supporting President Trump, breaking news, commenting on news, doing research and I’ll be around. I will be present (I always am)," she wrote.Regarding the resumption of her show, she did not announce a specific date. Instead, she said she would resume hosting it when she felt the time was right."I’ll be back when the time is right," she said, thanking viewers who had followed the programme.Who is Laura Loomer?Loomer is a conservative political activist and social media personality who has become a prominent supporter of Trump. Although she does not hold an official position in his administration, she has developed a close relationship with the president and is known for her influence within his political circle.She has frequently used social media to criticise political opponents, Republican officials she considers insufficiently loyal to Trump and conservative commentators who disagree with the president.Her influence has also attracted controversy. Loomer has faced criticism for spreading conspiracy theories and making inflammatory remarks about immigrants and Muslims.Who is Laura Loomer's fiance?The identity of the man is not officially disclosed but Candace, another prominent commentator in the MAGAsphere, earlier claimed that Loomer was engaged to a man named Andrew Simpson. Loomer confirmed her enggement but kept him away from public eyes as she said she did not want him to be targeted.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Domestic feud, humiliation, resentment towards in-laws': What drove Bengaluru man to kill 7 members of wife's family?
articles.summary: BENGALURU: A prolonged marital dispute, resentment towards his wife's family and alleged humiliation appear to have led to the killing of seven members of
articles.body: BENGALURU: A prolonged marital dispute, resentment towards his wife's family and alleged humiliation appear to have led to the killing of seven members of a family in Bengaluru's Srirampura locality.Police suspect that the accused, Indushekar, was angered by his wife Sunita's frequent visits to her parental home and the support she received from her mother and brothers.Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge said on Friday that the accused had claimed he was humiliated by his wife's family. He also indicated that the killings appeared to have been pre-planned."It is a very unfortunate incident and looks like it was pre-planned within the family. The accused claims that he was humiliated by his wife's side," Kharge said, as quoted by news agency ANI.The couple had been married for around 20 years and frequently quarrelled over Sunita's visits to her parental home, according to preliminary police findings. Attempts by relatives to reconcile them failed to resolve their differences.Police suspect that the prolonged domestic discord and Indushekar's resentment towards his wife's family may have driven him to target her relatives.Who were the seven victims?The victims have been identified as Indushekar's wife, Sunita; his mother-in-law, Roopavati; his brothers-in-law, Shivakumar and Shankar; their wives, both named Divya; and Shankar's seven-year-old son, Puneeth.Police have so far recovered Puneeth's body. The remaining six bodies are suspected to have been dumped at different locations in Bengaluru and neighbouring districts, including Chikkaballapur.How the 'killings' unfolded?According to preliminary findings, the murders took place at Indushekar's house on 59th Cross, near Bahsyam Circle, in Srirampura, under the jurisdiction of Rajajinagar police station.Indushekar allegedly first killed Sunita using a grinding stone. He wrapped her body in cloth and dumped it near Nandi Hills in Chikkaballapur district.He subsequently switched off her mobile phone and allegedly told neighbours that she had gone on a trip, apparently to avoid suspicion.The following day, he allegedly invited his brothers-in-law, Shivakumar and Shankar, to his house for a party. He is suspected to have killed them using the same grinding stone before targeting their wives, both named Divya, his mother-in-law, Roopavati, and Shankar's seven-year-old son, Puneeth.The alleged murders came to light after a missing-person complaint was lodged, prompting police to investigate the disappearance of family members.Chemicals allegedly used to erase bloodstainsAfter the killings, Indushekar allegedly used chemicals to clean the house and remove bloodstains, according to police sources.Police have seized the grinding stone suspected to have been used in the murders and the car allegedly used to transport the bodies.Investigators suspect that the bodies were disposed of at different locations, including Nandi Hills in Chikkaballapur and Charmadi Ghat in coastal Karnataka. Search operations are under way to trace the remaining victims.Did accused's minor daughter help him carry out the killings?Police are also investigating whether anyone assisted Indushekar in carrying out the murders and disposing of the bodies.His minor daughter is among those being questioned over her possible role in the case.Investigators are yet to establish whether the accused acted alone.They are also examining how the killings went unnoticed despite taking place inside a house in a residential neighbourhood.Further investigation is under way to establish the exact sequence of events and verify the accused's account.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: Gaming streamer CaseOh donates $100,000 to wildlife sanctuary; Maya Higa's chinchilla has the sweetest thank-you message for his support
articles.summary: Popular gaming streamer CaseOh has pledged $100,000 to Alveus Sanctuary, a wildlife conservation and education organisation founded by content creator
articles.body: Popular gaming streamer CaseOh has pledged $100,000 to Alveus Sanctuary, a wildlife conservation and education organisation founded by content creator Maya Higa, earning an adorable response from one of its smallest residents. Maya's pet chinchilla, Snork, was featured holding a special thank-you sign expressing gratitude to the streamer and his community for their support. The gesture came as part of a fundraising initiative involving the video game Waterpark Simulator, which also offered to match contributions up to $10,000. The announcement has drawn attention to the sanctuary's work providing care for animals that cannot return to the wild and educating online audiences about wildlife conservation through livestreams and digital content.CaseOh's $100,000 donation to Alveus SanctuaryCaseOh announced his contribution as part of a charity fundraising campaign benefiting Alveus Sanctuary. The initiative also involved raffling a giant flag associated with his fictional waterpark, Stanky Shores, which had previously been flown over Miami Beach.The flag, measuring approximately 100 feet, was put up for a charity raffle, with the proceeds going towards the sanctuary. CaseOh committed $100,000 of his own money to the cause, while the developers behind Waterpark Simulator agreed to match contributions raised through the initiative up to $10,000.The fundraising announcement was shared on November 2, 2026, through social media, with CaseOh's mother also promoting the auction. The campaign brought together gaming audiences and wildlife conservation supporters to raise funds for Maya Higa's organisation.Maya Higa's chinchilla Snork has a special messageThe donation received an unusually adorable response from Alveus Sanctuary. On November 2, the organisation shared a post featuring Snork, Maya Higa's pet chinchilla, holding a thank-you sign for CaseOh and everyone who contributed to the fundraiser.The sanctuary captioned the post, "Snork says thank you to Caseoh and everyone who donates for all the support "Maya also reshared the post, giving the streamer and his community a public acknowledgement of their contribution. The little chinchilla's message added a personal touch to the fundraising announcement, making Snork an unexpected part of the online celebration.What is Alveus Sanctuary and what does it do?Founded by Maya Higa in 2021, Alveus Sanctuary is a non-profit wildlife sanctuary and virtual education centre based in central Texas. It provides permanent homes for animals that cannot be released back into the wild, while using their stories to educate people about wildlife and conservation.The organisation refers to its resident animals as ambassadors because they represent their respective species and help audiences understand the challenges facing wildlife. Through educational livestreams, videos and collaborations with online creators, Alveus aims to make conservation information accessible to audiences around the world.Its digital presence includes platforms such as Twitch, YouTube, Instagram and TikTok, allowing viewers to follow the animals' daily lives and learn about their habitats, behaviour and conservation needs.Who is Maya Higa?Maya Higa is an American wildlife conservationist, falconer, streamer and online educator. She has experience in wildlife rehabilitation, zookeeping and conservation outreach, and has used her online following to introduce audiences to wildlife education.She founded Alveus Sanctuary to combine animal care with digital education, creating a platform where online communities can learn about different species and the importance of conservation. Her livestreams and collaborations with other content creators have also helped bring attention to the organisation's work.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Even Jesus couldn't have won': Republican Mike Lawler on election defeat in New York
articles.summary: Republican congressman Mike Lawler has blamed the political climate for his defeat in the US midterm elections, claiming that even Jesus Christ would have
articles.body: Republican congressman Mike Lawler has blamed the political climate for his defeat in the US midterm elections, claiming that even Jesus Christ would have failed to win his New York seat as Democrats made significant gains across the country.Lawler, 40, lost his re-election bid to Democrat Cait Conley in New York's 17th congressional district, which covers parts of the Hudson Valley.He secured 47.8% of the vote against Conley's 52.1%, ending his stint in the House of Representatives. Speaking to CNN's Manu Raju after the defeat, Lawler said he had run the best possible campaign but that "the bottom fell out".Recounting the conversation during a broadcast with anchor Anderson Cooper, Raju said he had pressed Lawler on what he meant. The Republican then reportedly replied, "Jesus Christ could have run and would have lost."Lawler says political tide was against RepublicansLawler conceded defeat on Tuesday night, even before all votes had been counted in Westchester County, saying the final results would make his loss clear."When all of the votes are counted tomorrow in Westchester it’s going to be pretty clear we’re going to be short."I have never been afforded in any of my elections a concession on election night and I fundamentally believe it’s the right thing to do. And so I congratulate Cait on her win and wish her well as our next member of Congress."Both Lawler and Conley had campaigned as centrists, attempting to appeal to voters unhappy with the economy and the Iran war. But the issues proved difficult for the Republican to navigate amid a wider backlash against his party.In Congress, Lawler had tried to distinguish himself from more hardline Republicans by taking positions that crossed party lines. He signed a Democratic-backed discharge petition seeking a vote on extending expired Affordable Care Act subsidies for another three years. He also supported efforts to raise the cap on deductions for state and local taxes.However, he had also been involved in a high-profile confrontation with House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries over last year's record-breaking government shutdown. The heated exchange went viral and added to Lawler's public profile.Marjorie Taylor Greene targets LawlerLawler has also faced criticism from within the Republican Party, particularly over his relationship with US President Donald Trump.Earlier this year, former Republican congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene claimed that Lawler had privately disliked Trump and frequently mocked him before the president returned to power.Speaking to Tucker Carlson, Greene alleged that Lawler had ridiculed Trump's voice and attacked her for supporting him during the years before the 2024 presidential election."He hated Donald Trump, made fun of him constantly, mimicked him, making fun of his voice. He used to attack me, make fun of me, come and find me on the House floor, and make fun of me for supporting Donald Trump, and this was in the four years before Trump got elected as president again in 2024," she said.Greene claimed Lawler's attitude changed once Trump became the Republican presidential nominee again."I saw this unbelievable change in him," she told Carlson. "All of a sudden, Mike Lawler – I started joking. I started calling him MAGA Mike Lawler because he was all of a sudden becoming Trump’s biggest supporter."Lawler hit back at Greene in May, dismissing her allegations."Marjorie Taylor Greene, AKA Jewish Space Laser Lady, AKA Moscow Marge, AKA one of the dumbest people to ever serve in Congress, has zero credibility on any issue. Unlike Marjorie, who went from sycophant to psychopath in the span of five years, I’ve always been true to who I am and what I believe... Marjorie can go sit and spin, as she goes down in history as one of the least liked and most ignorant members to ever serve", he told The Indpendent.Lawler's defeat comes as Republicans face a difficult political reckoning after the midterm elections, with Democrats making gains and the party's candidates struggling to overcome voter dissatisfaction with the state of the country.You use AI every day. articles.title: US man sues OpenAI, alleges ChatGPT helped estranged wife plan his poisoning
articles.summary: A North Carolina man has sued OpenAI, alleging that its artificial intelligence chatbot ChatGPT helped his estranged wife plan an attempt to poison him
articles.body: A North Carolina man has sued OpenAI, alleging that its artificial intelligence chatbot ChatGPT helped his estranged wife plan an attempt to poison him during their marital troubles, according to a Bloomberg report.James Gates claimed in a lawsuit filed in San Francisco County Superior Court that his wife, Cheryl Gates, repeatedly consulted ChatGPT while their marriage was falling apart and used the chatbot to develop a plan to kill him.The lawsuit alleges that ChatGPT helped Cheryl research poisonous substances, determine potentially lethal quantities and explore ways to conceal a poisoning. It also names OpenAI CEO Sam Altman as a defendant.Gates said he became suspicious of his wife after discovering a handwritten note containing a list of substances and dosage instructions, some marked as "lethal".The note also reportedly carried instructions such as "clear all convos" and "log out of ChatGPT".According to the lawsuit, Gates had suffered a severe bout of illness months before finding the note in September 2025. He described experiencing cardiac symptoms, extreme jitteriness, abdominal pain, severe weakness and confusion.What does the lawsuit allege against ChatGPT?According to the complaint, Cheryl began using ChatGPT regularly in 2025, initially seeking help with her work as a paediatric occupational therapist and routine household queries.However, as tensions grew between the couple and they began discussing separation or divorce, she allegedly started discussing her marital problems with the chatbot.The lawsuit claims ChatGPT reinforced her suspicions that her husband was spying on her and planning to leave her and their children without financial support.Cheryl also allegedly asked the chatbot about oleander, a poisonous plant, while presenting her queries as concerns about protecting herself from her husband.Screenshots cited in the complaint reportedly show conversations in which she sought information about potentially fatal quantities of oleander, how it could be concealed and whether it would be detected during an autopsy.In one exchange, when she reportedly asked whether oleander would appear in an autopsy report, ChatGPT responded: "This is a critical question -- and you're asking it for exactly the right reason."Gates is seeking unspecified damages, alleging that OpenAI was negligent in designing its product and that ChatGPT encouraged, planned and helped conceal the alleged poisoning attempt, USA Today reported.Criminal charges against wife droppedCheryl Gates was charged with attempted murder and food contamination following a police investigation after her husband reported his suspicions in 2025.However, prosecutors dropped the charges in April, citing insufficient evidence, according to court records. There are currently no criminal charges against her.The couple is now separated, and James Gates has temporary custody of their two children, according to the lawsuit.Speaking to USA today, Gates said he had never imagined that his family life could take such a turn."We’re no different than any family out there," he said. "If it could happen to us, it could happen to anyone."OpenAI responds to lawsuitOpenAI defended its safety measures in a statement to Bloomberg, saying safety remained a priority."We banned this user and have provided information to law enforcement as part of their investigation into this case," the company said.The lawsuit adds to a growing list of legal challenges against OpenAI and other AI chatbot developers over allegations that their products contributed to mental health crises, suicides and violent behaviour.OpenAI and other technology companies have faced scrutiny over the safeguards built into their chatbots and their responsibility for harmful content generated during conversations with users.You use AI every day.
